title: Feature: Learnings-aware planner (dedup against rejected approaches + cite prior rationale)
summary: Next self-learning feature (user pick, 2026-06-08): make the planner actually anti-repeat losing approaches. Gap: self-learn-planner skill already calls get_learnings(), but the strongest anti-repeat signal (loser rationale) is buried in nested verdicts[].losers[].reason and in genuine dead-end failures, so the planner doesn't reliably dedup against it, and nothing forces it to cite WHY a past approach lost. Two-part build: (a) DAEMON — get_learnings() gains a flat, pre-digested rejected[] list = verdict losers ({approach, reason, beatenBy, source:'verdict'}) + genuine dead-end failures (EXCLUDING notes matching superseded/duplicate/consolidated), one-pass scannable; unit-tested. (b) SKILL — self-learn-planner step 1+4 build a rejected-approaches ledger from rejected[], dedup every candidate initiative against it, and when a proposal is adjacent to a settled question cite the prior verdict rationale in the new task description. Daemon part is the verifiable contract (46 unit-test suite); skill depends on the new field.
